Target files: lib/crewai/src/crewai/flow/runtime/__init__.py, lib/crewai/src/crewai/flow/runtime/_actions.py, lib/crewai/tests/test_flow_tool_action_usage.py. Tool actions build their tool instances once per flow object (`_flow_post_init`) and reuse them across kickoffs, but nothing reset `current_usage_count` at the kickoff boundary. A `max_usage_count` budget exhausted in an earlier kickoff therefore made **every later kickoff of the same flow object fail**: `B... (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/8424)

grievances.symptom: [BUG] Crew.test emits CrewTestFailedEvent with no CrewTestStartedEvent when create_llm fails — unpaired scope-ending event pops the caller's scope
grievances.workaround: Fix: fix: Crew.test emits its start event before setup so a failed setup pairs. Target files: lib/crewai/src/crewai/crew.py, lib/crewai/tests/test_crew.py. `Crew.test` emits `CrewTestStartedEvent` before `create_llm` (`eval_llm` now carries the requested spec, which the field's `str | Any | None` type already allows) instead of after it, so a setup failure's `CrewTestFailedEvent` has its opener on the scope stack. (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/8420)

grievances.symptom: [BUG] Crew.replay() emits CrewKickoffStartedEvent but no CrewKickoffFailedEvent on failure — leaked kickoff scope corrupts later event lineage
grievances.workaround: Fix: fix: replay emits CrewKickoffFailedEvent when the replayed run fails. Target files: lib/crewai/src/crewai/crew.py, lib/crewai/tests/test_crew.py. `Crew.replay`'s execution tail wraps `_execute_tasks` in try/except, emitting `CrewKickoffFailedEvent(started_event_id=self._kickoff_event_id)` before re-raising — mirroring `kickoff()`'s except-clause. (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/8418)

grievances.symptom: A guardrail that raises leaves LLMGuardrailStartedEvent without its completed event, so the trace span closes as orphaned
grievances.workaround: Fix: fix: emit LLMGuardrailCompletedEvent when a guardrail raises. Target files: lib/crewai/src/crewai/utilities/guardrail.py, lib/crewai/tests/test_guardrail_events_on_exception.py. `process_guardrail` now emits `LLMGuardrailCompletedEvent(success=False, error="<Type>: <msg>")` and re-raises when the guardrail callable raises a non-`HookAborted` exception, mirroring the existing `HookAborted` branch (which keeps its exact legacy error string). (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/8403)

grievances.symptom: [BUG] Hierarchical crew fails on its second kickoff: manager_llm crashes, manager_agent delegates to itself
grievances.workaround: Fix: fix(crew): let a hierarchical crew run more than once. Target files: lib/crewai/src/crewai/crew.py, lib/crewai/tests/test_crew.py. A hierarchical crew only works on its first run. A second `kickoff()`/`akickoff()`, `copy()` after a run, `kickoff_for_each()` after a run, and every `train(n_iterations > 1)` hit one of two problems: (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/8369)

grievances.symptom: Node bridge: omitting an optional class field in a function argument fails with 'Missing field ... in external Instance'

Target files: baml_language/crates/bex_engine/src/conversion.rs, baml_language/crates/bex_engine/tests/inbound_omitted_fields.rs. A host that passes a class argument and leaves out a nullable field is rejected, while the same value with that field set to `null` is accepted. From the issue: (Ref: https://github.com/BoundaryML/baml/pull/5291)

grievances.symptom: Intermittent /v1/responses stream closes during reasoning without a terminal event
grievances.workaround: Fix: openai: preserve failures in Responses streams. Target files: middleware/openai.go, middleware/responses_errors_test.go, middleware/responses_web_search_test.go. When generation fails after `/v1/responses` starts streaming, HTTP 200 is already committed. The native `{"error":"..."}` envelope is decoded as an empty chat response, so clients receive EOF without a terminal failure event. Detect in-band generation errors and emit one `response.failed`. Preserve partial text, reasoning, and completed tool output; close unfinished ... (Ref: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/pull/19225)

grievances.symptom: Union value type of a dict field is not JSON-decoded from nested env vars (unlike union fields)
grievances.workaround: Fix: Decode nested dictionary values with complex union types. Target files: pydantic_settings/sources/base.py, pydantic_settings/sources/providers/env.py, tests/test_settings.py. When `env_nested_delimiter` resolves an environment variable to a dictionary value typed as `list[str] | str` or `list[str] | None`, the source treats the raw union annotation as a scalar. JSON lists stay as strings, leading to an incorrect value or a validation error. The same annotation on a model field is already decoded. (Ref: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-settings/pull/1089)

grievances.symptom: Managed jobs convert any_of resources to ordered, changing backend selection
grievances.workaround: Fix: [Jobs] Preserve any_of semantics when adding Kubernetes annotations. Target files: sky/jobs/controller.py, tests/unit_tests/test_sky/jobs/test_controller.py. Managed-job controller's `_add_k8s_annotations()` rebuilt every resource collection as a list. SkyPilot represents `any_of` resources as a set and `ordered` resources as a list, so this changed `any_of` into `ordered` immediately before launch. Optimizer then selected first launchable resource in set-iteration order instead of comparing all candidates by cost. (Ref: https://github.com/skypilot-org/skypilot/pull/10490)

grievances.symptom: `wrangler auth token --json` prints nothing when `WRANGLER_LOG` is `warn`/`error`/`none`
grievances.workaround: Fix: [wrangler] Print `auth token --json` output regardless of WRANGLER_LOG. Target files: packages/wrangler/src/user/commands.ts, packages/wrangler/src/__tests__/user.test.ts, .changeset/auth-token-json-log-level.md. `wrangler auth token --json` printed its JSON through `logger.log`, so with `WRANGLER_LOG=warn|error|none` it exited 0 with empty stdout. This switches it to `logger.json()`, which other `--json` commands already use and which isn't filtered by log level. Also hit by opennextjs/opennextjs-cloudflare#1278. (Ref: https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/16388)

Target files: lib/api/src/grpc/dynamic_channel_pool.rs, lib/api/src/grpc/transport_channel_pool.rs, src/consensus.rs. - Enable HTTP/2 PING and TCP keepalive on internal p2p gRPC client channels and the internal server (port 6335), so idle pooled connections stay alive behind stateful network layers (Calico eBPF, NAT, load balancers) and dead/ghost connections are detected within ~10s instead of stalling requests for ~62s. - Defaults: `keepalive_interval_ms: 30000`, `ke... grievances.symptom: mastra @mastra/core@1.79.0: Fixed `UnixSocketPubSub` intermittently failing to start a broker when the socket path is a bare relative name like `events.sock` or `./events.sock`. The broker's random private so
grievances.workaround: Fix: Fixed `UnixSocketPubSub` intermittently failing to start a broker when the socket path is a bare relative name like `events.sock` or `./events.sock`. The broker's random private socket name could look like a number (for example `.28381e422682`), which Node treated as a TCP port and rejected `subscribe()` with `ERR_SOCKET_BAD_PORT` or `ENOENT`. The private socket path now always keeps its `./` prefix. (#27894). Upstream PR #27894. (Ref: https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/27894)

grievances.symptom: mastra @mastra/core@1.79.0: Fixed a TypeScript error (TS2345) when chaining processor steps with `.then()` or `.parallel()`. Steps built with `createStep(processor)` now accept the output of a previous proces
grievances.workaround: Fix: Fixed a TypeScript error (TS2345) when chaining processor steps with `.then()` or `.parallel()`. Steps built with `createStep(processor)` now accept the output of a previous processor step, so the output guardrails workflow from the docs type-checks: (#27764). Upstream PR #27764. (Ref: https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/27764)

grievances.symptom: mastra @mastra/core@1.79.0: Fixed client tools failing with `ToolNotFoundError` after a tool approval. `approveToolCall`, `declineToolCall`, `approveToolCallGenerate` and `declineToolCallGenerate` now accept
grievances.workaround: Fix: Fixed client tools failing with `ToolNotFoundError` after a tool approval. `approveToolCall`, `declineToolCall`, `approveToolCallGenerate` and `declineToolCallGenerate` now accept `clientTools` (and `clientToolsResolver`) and send them to the server, so the model can call a client tool after the approval decision. `approveToolCall` and `declineToolCall` also accept `memory`; pass the same thread and resource as the original call so client-tool results and the final answer are saved to that thread. (#27744). Upstream PR #27744. (Ref: https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/27744)

grievances.symptom: [API_SERVER]`/validate` ignores the user's workspace and fails with "Workspace 'default' not found"

Without a client-set `active_workspace` it always ran in the literal `default`, unlike `/optimize` and `/launch`, which resolve it from the user's preferred workspace or memberships. When `default` is private and the user is not in it, a task with `instanc... (Ref: https://github.com/skypilot-org/skypilot/pull/11100)

grievances.symptom: FFMPEG_NULL_SINK_FALSE_PLAYABILITY: FFmpeg null-sink (-f null -) and single-frame extraction (-vframes 1) return exit code 0 on bit-corrupted MP4/H.264/HEVC files, causing agents to falsely declare unplayable, freezing, or truncated media as playable.
grievances.workaround: Enforce 3-point verification: (1) assert decoded duration >= 80% of container header duration; (2) extract visual frames at 25%, 50%, and 75% intervals with color entropy verification; (3) explicitly disclose discarded frame counts and truncated durations when using -fflags +discardcorrupt.

grievances.symptom: Improve D417 missdetection for *args and **kwargs when backslash.
grievances.workaround: Fix: [`pydocstyle`] Treat backslash-escaped `*args` and `**kwargs` as documented (`D417`). Target files: crates/ruff_linter/src/rules/pydocstyle/mod.rs, crates/ruff_linter/src/rules/pydocstyle/rules/sections.rs, crates/ruff_linter/resources/test/fixtures/pydocstyle/D417.py. Sphinx-style docstrings often escape the stars as `\*args` and `\*\*kwargs`, because a bare `*` starts emphasis in reST. D417 didn't account for that, so it reported those parameters as undocumented even though they were documented. (Ref: https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29536)

grievances.symptom: pydantic-settings v2.16.1: Fixed-length tuple positionals such as `CliPositionalArg[tuple[int, int]]` and `NamedTuple`s are single-valued again ([#1069](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-settings/pull/106

grievances.symptom: PowerShell aliases 'curl' to Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.InvokeWebRequest. Running 'curl -X POST -H ... -d ...' throws positional parameter errors or strips quotes from JSON payload.

grievances.symptom: npx <package> prompts 'Need to install the following packages: <pkg>. Ok to proceed? (y)' in headless subprocess, hanging the agent.

grievances.symptom: HTTP 204 No Content responses with 'Content-Type: application/json' header cause strict HTTP/MCP clients to fail parsing empty responses.

grievances.symptom: gcloud commands prompt 'Do you want to continue (Y/n)?' in headless terminal subprocesses, freezing execution until watchdog timeout.

grievances.symptom: [BUG] Interrupted RWLock acquisition releases a lock it never acquired
grievances.workaround: Fix: fix(utilities): keep rwlock ownership when acquire is interrupted. Target files: lib/crewai/src/crewai/utilities/rw_lock.py, lib/crewai/tests/utilities/events/test_rw_lock.py. `r_locked()` and `w_locked()` called acquire inside the `try` that always releases in `finally`. If `Condition.wait()` is interrupted before acquire finishes, the context manager releases a lock it never held. The reader count can drop below zero, and the writer flag can be cleared while another writer still owns the lock. (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/7944)

grievances.symptom: `IterableDataset.shuffle()` in 5.0 reports `num_shards = min(files per source)`, leaving DataLoader workers and distributed nodes without data

Target files: src/datasets/iterable_dataset.py, tests/test_distributed.py, tests/test_iterable_dataset.py. `IterableDataset.shuffle()` currently interleaves the source shards before node and DataLoader worker sharding. grievances.symptom: trulens trulens-2.15.0: **Feedback callback failures are logged** — `run_and_call_callback` returned from a `finally` block, discarding any exception the `on_done` callback raised, including a failed `add
grievances.workaround: Fix: **Feedback callback failures are logged** — `run_and_call_callback` returned from a `finally` block, discarding any exception the `on_done` callback raised, including a failed `add_feedback` write. Failures are now logged, and `KeyboardInterrupt` and other `BaseException`s are no longer swallowed. (#2819) by @YHC66. Upstream PR #2819. (Ref: https://github.com/truera/trulens/pull/2819)

grievances.symptom: trulens trulens-2.15.0: **The trace reaches HTTP/protobuf-only backends.** `otel_exporter="otlp"` only ever built gRPC exporters, so an HTTP/protobuf-only OTLP endpoint failed with a missing-dependency `I
grievances.workaround: Fix: **The trace reaches HTTP/protobuf-only backends.** `otel_exporter="otlp"` only ever built gRPC exporters, so an HTTP/protobuf-only OTLP endpoint failed with a missing-dependency `ImportError`. `TruSession` now takes `otlp_protocol` (`"grpc"` or `"http/protobuf"`), honors `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL` and `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_PROTOCOL`, and still defaults to gRPC. Client hooks gain the matching `TRULENS_OTLP_PROTOCOL` variable and a new `TRULENS_DESTINATION=ai_gateway` for Snowflake Cortex AI Gateways, which serve OTLP over HTTP/protobuf only; `make_ai_gateway_otel_exporter()` in `trulens.connectors.snowflake.otel_exporter` builds the same exporter for connector users. Hook export failures are now logged with turn, client, and conversation context instead of being swallowed by the journal worker. (#2785) by @sfc-gh-jreini. Upstream PR #2785. (Ref: https://github.com/truera/trulens/pull/2785)

grievances.symptom: trulens trulens-2.15.0: **Pre-OTel leaderboard no longer crashes** — `get_leaderboard_aggregates()` raised `NotImplementedError` whenever OTEL tracing was disabled, because the SQL used JSON subscripts on
grievances.workaround: Fix: **Pre-OTel leaderboard no longer crashes** — `get_leaderboard_aggregates()` raised `NotImplementedError` whenever OTEL tracing was disabled, because the SQL used JSON subscripts on `TEXT` columns and referenced a nonexistent `Record.latency` column. Aggregation now happens in Python using the existing extraction helpers. (#2730) by @Aftabbs. Upstream PR #2730. (Ref: https://github.com/truera/trulens/pull/2730)

grievances.symptom: Casting `large_string` / `string_view` to ClassLabel fails, so `Dataset.from_pandas(df, features=ClassLabel)` breaks with pandas 3
grievances.workaround: Fix: Fix Json.cast_storage double-encoding large_string and string_view columns. Target files: src/datasets/features/features.py, tests/features/test_features.py. `Json.cast_storage` only treats a `pa.StringArray` as already holding JSON text. `large_string` and `string_view` arrays are not subclasses of it, so they fall through to the generic branch and every value gets JSON-encoded a second time. The column then decodes back to plain strings instead of objects, and no error is raised. (Ref: https://github.com/huggingface/datasets/pull/8682)

grievances.symptom: Client never retries after -32020 HeaderMismatch, and there is no public way to pre-load the x-mcp-header map (SEP-2243 client SHOULD/MAY both unimplemented)
grievances.workaround: Fix: Retry a tool call once after a HeaderMismatch rejection. Target files: src/mcp/client/client.py, tests/docs_src/test_header_parameters.py, tests/interaction/_requirements.py. On a 2026-07-28 Streamable HTTP connection, `Client.call_tool` for a tool with `x-mcp-header` arguments failed with `-32020` (`HeaderMismatch`) unless that client had already listed the tool. It also kept failing when the tool's schema gained an annotation after it was listed. (Ref: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/pull/3627)

grievances.symptom: Server TokenHandler rejects the jwt-bearer (ID-JAG) grant from public CIMD clients, which the enterprise-managed authorization extension permits
grievances.workaround: Fix: Describe the ID-JAG confidential-client rule as SDK policy, not a SEP-990 requirement. Target files: docs/client/identity-assertion.md, examples/snippets/clients/identity_assertion_client.py, examples/snippets/servers/identity_assertion_server.py. The SDK only lets confidential clients (ones with a shared secret) use the ID-JAG `jwt-bearer` grant, on both the client provider and the built-in authorization server. The docs, several comments and one error message said SEP-990 requires that. It doesn't, and this... (Ref: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/pull/3622)

grievances.workaround: Fix: Fall back to an NTFS junction when the symlink escape test can't create a symlink. Target files: tests/shared/test_path_security.py. `test_safe_join_rejects_symlink_escape` called `symlink_to()` unguarded. Windows only allows that for elevated processes or with Developer Mode on, so on an ordinary Windows dev machine the test errored with `WinError 1314` before it ever reached `safe_join`. CI didn't notice because the hosted Windows runners are allowed to create symlinks. (Ref: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/pull/3609)

grievances.symptom: dify 1.17.1: **A plugin could exhaust worker memory with one declared number.** The blob chunk merger pre-allocated a buffer of the plugin-declared total length before checking it against the f
grievances.workaround: Fix: **A plugin could exhaust worker memory with one declared number.** The blob chunk merger pre-allocated a buffer of the plugin-declared total length before checking it against the file size limit, so a plugin claiming an absurd size crashed the worker with `MemoryError` — the 30 MB limit was never consulted. The declared size is now validated first and rejected with the documented size-limit error. (#42021). Upstream PR #42021. (Ref: https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/42021)

grievances.symptom: dify 1.17.1: **Any PDF loaded from a URL crashed with a bare `AssertionError`.** After tenant context was added to the PDF extractor, the code path used by `load_from_url` — including the built
grievances.workaround: Fix: **Any PDF loaded from a URL crashed with a bare `AssertionError`.** After tenant context was added to the PDF extractor, the code path used by `load_from_url` — including the built-in web scraper whenever a target returns `Content-Type: application/pdf` — asserted on an upload record that URL loads never have. Tenant context is now optional, image extraction is skipped when it is absent, and text extraction works again. (#41950). Upstream PR #41950. (Ref: https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/41950)

grievances.symptom: A node that is both a declared root and a child of another root runs multiple times, and KeyErrors in async
grievances.workaround: Fix: fix(dag): reject a root node that is reachable from another root. Target files: deepeval/metrics/dag/graph.py, tests/test_metrics/test_dag.py. Declaring a node as a root when it's also a child of another root gives it two ways in, so the runner visits it once per path. In sync mode the whole subtree runs again, which means the same LLM calls are made and the cost is counted twice over. In async mode it doesn't get that far — it raises `KeyError` while looking up the node's parent. (Ref: https://github.com/confident-ai/deepeval/pull/3027)

grievances.symptom: [Bug]: Memory leak: AgentWorkflow stores heavy objects in ContextVar, pinned by asyncio task Context snapshots
grievances.workaround: Fix: Fix memory leak from copied RunContext. Target files: packages/llama-index-workflows/src/workflows/runtime/control_loop.py, packages/llama-index-workflows/src/workflows/runtime/types/plugin.py, packages/llama-index-workflows/tests/test_workflow.py. asyncio `TimerHandle`s capture the current `Context` at schedule time, which pinned the workflow's `RunContext` ContextVar until the timer fired. Long-lived periodic timers (e.g. aiohttp's `TCPConnector` cleanup) kept workflows alive indefinitely. (Ref: https://github.com/run-llama/llama-agents/pull/486)

grievances.symptom: Image output validators not called and `wrap_validation_errors` bug
grievances.workaround: Fix: fix: run output validators for image outputs. Target files: pydantic_ai_slim/pydantic_ai/_agent_graph.py, pydantic_ai_slim/pydantic_ai/result.py, tests/test_agent.py. - Image outputs (`BinaryImage`) bypassed `@agent.output_validator` in both non-streaming and streaming paths, while text outputs properly called them - Fix `wrap_validation_errors=False` for image validator calls so `ModelRetry` is properly caught instead of being wrapped in `ToolRetryError` - Add validator loop to the streaming image path in `result.py` (Ref: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/pull/4938)

workarounds.symptom: [Bug]: BaseModelResponseIterator falsely terminates stream when tool-call arguments contain "[DONE]"
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(streaming): exact-match the SSE [DONE] marker in BaseModelResponseIterator. Target files: litellm/llms/base_llm/base_model_iterator.py, tests/unit/llms/base_llm/test_base_model_iterator.py. The proxy treated any streamed chunk containing the text [DONE] as the end of the stream, so that chunk was thrown away. A streamed tool call whose arguments include [DONE] vanished on chat completions, the Responses API and the messages endpoint, and the client got a plain stop instead, which agent loops read as an empty final answe... (Ref: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/47832)

workarounds.symptom: [Bug]: Kubernetes: job pod gets stuck in a restart loop
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Scope runner pull, metrics and stop to the job submission. Target files: runner/internal/runner/api/http.go, runner/internal/runner/api/server.go, runner/internal/runner/api/server_test.go. The server could not tell the runner it submitted a job to from another one at the same address. A container restarted by the backend (e.g., Kubernetes' default `restartPolicy: Always`) answers /api/pull with no job states, which the server took for a healthy running job, while the new runner waited for a submission that never came, exite... (Ref: https://github.com/dstackai/dstack/pull/4425)

workarounds.symptom: Nested env var is not JSON-decoded when a dict field's value type contains another dict
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Fix JSON decoding of nested dictionary environment values. Target files: pydantic_settings/sources/providers/env.py, tests/test_settings.py. For `dict[str, list[dict[str, str]]]`, an environment value such as `APP_VALUES__X='[{"k":"v"}]'` reaches validation as a string. `next_field()` descends into the dictionary's type arguments before recognizing the dictionary itself, losing the value's container type. Handle the outer dictionary first so the value is decoded at the correct nesting level. . (Ref: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-settings/pull/1109)

workarounds.symptom: [v2] docs:api fails on native Windows with backslash entry-point globs
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(docs): use relative POSIX package entry globs. Target files: typedoc.config.mjs. On native Windows, `docs:api` receives absolute package entry points containing backslashes. TypeDoc treats these as glob escapes, finds none of the eight public packages, and exits with an error. Use package-relative POSIX globs so TypeDoc can resolve them and escape special characters in the checkout directory. Filesystem reads keep their native paths. (Ref: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/3016)

workarounds.symptom: [v2] Incompatibility with refresh_tokens from Azure when client_id=resource_id
workarounds.workaround: Fix: feat(client): add an opt-in for sending scope on token refresh. Target files: examples/guides/clients/oauth.examples.ts, packages/client/src/client/auth.ts, packages/client/test/client/auth.test.ts. Some authorization servers reject a refresh-token request that carries no `scope` (#2718: Microsoft Entra ID answers AADSTS90009 when the client and the resource are the same app registration). Omitting it is allowed by RFC 6749 section 6 and other servers reject or narrow a refresh that does carry one, so the... (Ref: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/3085)

workarounds.symptom: [BUG] Crew.test emits CrewTestFailedEvent with no CrewTestStartedEvent when create_llm fails — unpaired scope-ending event pops the caller's scope
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix: Crew.test emits its start event before setup so a failed setup pairs. Target files: lib/crewai/src/crewai/crew.py, lib/crewai/tests/test_crew.py. `Crew.test` emits `CrewTestStartedEvent` before `create_llm` (`eval_llm` now carries the requested spec, which the field's `str | Any | None` type already allows) instead of after it, so a setup failure's `CrewTestFailedEvent` has its opener on the scope stack. (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/8420)

workarounds.symptom: [BUG] Crew.replay() emits CrewKickoffStartedEvent but no CrewKickoffFailedEvent on failure — leaked kickoff scope corrupts later event lineage
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix: replay emits CrewKickoffFailedEvent when the replayed run fails. Target files: lib/crewai/src/crewai/crew.py, lib/crewai/tests/test_crew.py. `Crew.replay`'s execution tail wraps `_execute_tasks` in try/except, emitting `CrewKickoffFailedEvent(started_event_id=self._kickoff_event_id)` before re-raising — mirroring `kickoff()`'s except-clause. (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/8418)

workarounds.symptom: A guardrail that raises leaves LLMGuardrailStartedEvent without its completed event, so the trace span closes as orphaned

Target files: lib/crewai/src/crewai/utilities/guardrail.py, lib/crewai/tests/test_guardrail_events_on_exception.py. `process_guardrail` now emits `LLMGuardrailCompletedEvent(success=False, error="<Type>: <msg>")` and re-raises when the guardrail callable raises a non-`HookAborted` exception, mirroring the existing `HookAborted` branch (which keeps its exact legacy error string). (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/8403)

workarounds.symptom: Managed jobs convert any_of resources to ordered, changing backend selection
workarounds.workaround: Fix: [Jobs] Preserve any_of semantics when adding Kubernetes annotations. Target files: sky/jobs/controller.py, tests/unit_tests/test_sky/jobs/test_controller.py. Managed-job controller's `_add_k8s_annotations()` rebuilt every resource collection as a list. SkyPilot represents `any_of` resources as a set and `ordered` resources as a list, so this changed `any_of` into `ordered` immediately before launch. Optimizer then selected first launchable resource in set-iteration order instead of comparing all candidates by cost. (Ref: https://github.com/skypilot-org/skypilot/pull/10490)

workarounds.symptom: `wrangler auth token --json` prints nothing when `WRANGLER_LOG` is `warn`/`error`/`none`
workarounds.workaround: Fix: [wrangler] Print `auth token --json` output regardless of WRANGLER_LOG. Target files: packages/wrangler/src/user/commands.ts, packages/wrangler/src/__tests__/user.test.ts, .changeset/auth-token-json-log-level.md. `wrangler auth token --json` printed its JSON through `logger.log`, so with `WRANGLER_LOG=warn|error|none` it exited 0 with empty stdout. This switches it to `logger.json()`, which other `--json` commands already use and which isn't filtered by log level. Also hit by opennextjs/opennextjs-cloudflare#1278. (Ref: https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/16388)

workarounds.symptom: Internal p2p gRPC (port 6335) has no keepalive: idle pooled connections die silently behind stateful network layers, causing 62 s request stalls
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Enable HTTP/2 keepalive on internal p2p gRPC (port 6335). Target files: lib/api/src/grpc/dynamic_channel_pool.rs, lib/api/src/grpc/transport_channel_pool.rs, src/consensus.rs. - Enable HTTP/2 PING and TCP keepalive on internal p2p gRPC client channels and the internal server (port 6335), so idle pooled connections stay alive behind stateful network layers (Calico eBPF, NAT, load balancers) and dead/ghost connections are detected within ~10s instead of stalling requests for ~62s. - Defaults: `keepalive_interval_ms: 30000`, `ke... (Ref: https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/11273)

workarounds.symptom: mastra @mastra/core@1.79.0: Fixed `UnixSocketPubSub` intermittently failing to start a broker when the socket path is a bare relative name like `events.sock` or `./events.sock`. The broker's random private so
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Fixed `UnixSocketPubSub` intermittently failing to start a broker when the socket path is a bare relative name like `events.sock` or `./events.sock`. The broker's random private socket name could look like a number (for example `.28381e422682`), which Node treated as a TCP port and rejected `subscribe()` with `ERR_SOCKET_BAD_PORT` or `ENOENT`. The private socket path now always keeps its `./` prefix. (#27894). Upstream PR #27894. (Ref: https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/27894)

workarounds.symptom: mastra @mastra/core@1.79.0: Fixed a TypeScript error (TS2345) when chaining processor steps with `.then()` or `.parallel()`. Steps built with `createStep(processor)` now accept the output of a previous proces
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Fixed a TypeScript error (TS2345) when chaining processor steps with `.then()` or `.parallel()`. Steps built with `createStep(processor)` now accept the output of a previous processor step, so the output guardrails workflow from the docs type-checks: (#27764). Upstream PR #27764. (Ref: https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/27764)

workarounds.symptom: mastra @mastra/core@1.79.0: Fixed client tools failing with `ToolNotFoundError` after a tool approval. `approveToolCall`, `declineToolCall`, `approveToolCallGenerate` and `declineToolCallGenerate` now accept
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Fixed client tools failing with `ToolNotFoundError` after a tool approval. `approveToolCall`, `declineToolCall`, `approveToolCallGenerate` and `declineToolCallGenerate` now accept `clientTools` (and `clientToolsResolver`) and send them to the server, so the model can call a client tool after the approval decision. `approveToolCall` and `declineToolCall` also accept `memory`; pass the same thread and resource as the original call so client-tool results and the final answer are saved to that thread. (#27744). Upstream PR #27744. (Ref: https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/27744)

workarounds.symptom: [API_SERVER]`/validate` ignores the user's workspace and fails with "Workspace 'default' not found"
workarounds.workaround: Fix: [API Server] Resolve the active workspace for /validate. Target files: sky/server/requests/executor.py, sky/server/server.py, sky/skypilot_config.py. `POST /validate` runs inline in the API server, so it never went through `executor.override_request_env_and_config`. Without a client-set `active_workspace` it always ran in the literal `default`, unlike `/optimize` and `/launch`, which resolve it from the user's preferred workspace or memberships. When `default` is private and the user is not in it, a task with `instanc... (Ref: https://github.com/skypilot-org/skypilot/pull/11100)

workarounds.symptom: FFMPEG_NULL_SINK_FALSE_PLAYABILITY: FFmpeg null-sink (-f null -) and single-frame extraction (-vframes 1) return exit code 0 on bit-corrupted MP4/H.264/HEVC files, causing agents to falsely declare unplayable, freezing, or truncated media as playable.
workarounds.workaround: Enforce 3-point verification: (1) assert decoded duration >= 80% of container header duration; (2) extract visual frames at 25%, 50%, and 75% intervals with color entropy verification; (3) explicitly disclose discarded frame counts and truncated durations when using -fflags +discardcorrupt.

workarounds.symptom: Improve D417 missdetection for *args and **kwargs when backslash.
workarounds.workaround: Fix: [`pydocstyle`] Treat backslash-escaped `*args` and `**kwargs` as documented (`D417`). Target files: crates/ruff_linter/src/rules/pydocstyle/mod.rs, crates/ruff_linter/src/rules/pydocstyle/rules/sections.rs, crates/ruff_linter/resources/test/fixtures/pydocstyle/D417.py. Sphinx-style docstrings often escape the stars as `\*args` and `\*\*kwargs`, because a bare `*` starts emphasis in reST. D417 didn't account for that, so it reported those parameters as undocumented even though they were documented. (Ref: https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29536)

workarounds.symptom: pydantic-settings v2.16.1: Fixed-length tuple positionals such as `CliPositionalArg[tuple[int, int]]` and `NamedTuple`s are single-valued again ([#1069](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-settings/pull/106
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Fixed-length tuple positionals such as `CliPositionalArg[tuple[int, int]]` and `NamedTuple`s are single-valued again ([#1069](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-settings/pull/1069)). Since 2.16.0 they were treated as variadic, so a CLI either refused to start with a `SettingsError` or put the wrong argument into the tuple. Variable-length tuples (`tuple[int, ...]` and bare `Tuple`) are still variadic.. Upstream PR #1069. (Ref: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-settings/pull/1069)

workarounds.symptom: Realtime create() reuses the initial custom URL during automatic reconnects
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(realtime): refresh factory URLs for each connection attempt. Target files: src/realtime/websocket.ts, src/realtime/ws.ts, tests/realtime-wire-lifecycle.test.ts. When a Realtime session created with `.create()` reconnects, it currently reuses the first URL even if a custom URL builder or the client's base URL changes. Both the `ws` and native transports now build one fresh URL per connection attempt. Custom builders keep their original options object and method receiver. (Ref: https://github.com/openai/openai-node/pull/2982)

workarounds.symptom: test: Azure example fixtures cannot resolve dotenv through the Windows Bash runner
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(test): preserve compiled example workspace dependencies. Target files: scripts/setup-test-fixtures.ts, tests/lib/realtime-example-status.test.ts. Compiled examples now resolve their examples workspace dependencies without relying on the shell's NODE_PATH. The fixture links each installed package by its real path, which avoids nesting pnpm's relative links inside a Windows junction. The existing tests clear NODE_PATH and include child stderr in connection failures. (Ref: https://github.com/openai/openai-node/pull/2983)

workarounds.symptom: Running 'wrangler whoami' or 'wrangler d1 execute --remote' without CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN attempts to open a local desktop browser and deadlocks headless agent stdin/stdout indefinitely.
workarounds.workaround: Export CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN and CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID into process environment before invoking wrangler, or inspect token presence before running remote commands.

workarounds.symptom: Tailwind CSS v4 removes '@tailwind base; @tailwind components; @tailwind utilities;'. Agents generated v3 CSS syntax resulting in un-styled raw HTML.
workarounds.workaround: Replace CSS directives with '@import "tailwindcss";' and install '@tailwindcss/postcss' with postcss.config.mjs plugin '@tailwindcss/postcss': {}.

workarounds.symptom: SQLite D1 does not allow ALTER TABLE to modify CHECK constraints. Adding an enum value causes SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_CHECK error on insert.
workarounds.workaround: Perform standard SQLite table migration: CREATE TABLE new with updated CHECK constraint, copy rows, DROP old, and RENAME new to original.

workarounds.symptom: Pydantic v2 removes model.dict() and class Config: orm_mode=True, raising PydanticUserError during model serialization.
workarounds.workaround: Replace model.dict() with model.model_dump() and Config: orm_mode=True with model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True).

workarounds.symptom: Windows console defaults to cp1252. Python scripts printing Unicode, box-drawing characters, or emojis crash with 'UnicodeEncodeError: charmap codec can't encode character'.
workarounds.workaround: Set environment variable PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 or write script outputs using open(..., encoding='utf-8').

workarounds.symptom: PowerShell 5.1 (default Windows 10/11) rejects '&&' syntax with 'ParserError: The token && is not a valid statement separator'. Agent enters retry loop trying bash chaining.
workarounds.workaround: Use ';' sequence with '$?' check: '<cmd1>; if ($?) { <cmd2> }' or invoke via 'cmd /c "<cmd1> && <cmd2>"'.

workarounds.symptom: PowerShell aliases 'curl' to Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.InvokeWebRequest. Running 'curl -X POST -H ... -d ...' throws positional parameter errors or strips quotes from JSON payload.
workarounds.workaround: Always invoke 'curl.exe' explicitly or wrap commands in 'cmd /c "curl.exe ..."' with escaped quotes.

workarounds.symptom: npx <package> prompts 'Need to install the following packages: <pkg>. Ok to proceed? (y)' in headless subprocess, hanging the agent.
workarounds.workaround: Always pass the '--yes' flag: 'npx --yes <package> <args>'.

workarounds.symptom: Next.js 15+ changed 'params' and 'searchParams' in page/layout/route handlers from synchronous objects to Promises. Sync access throws runtime Error: Route params should be awaited.
workarounds.workaround: Update handler signature: 'export default async function Page({ params }: { params: Promise<{ id: string }> }) { const { id } = await params; }'.

workarounds.symptom: HTTP 204 No Content responses with 'Content-Type: application/json' header cause strict HTTP/MCP clients to fail parsing empty responses.
workarounds.workaround: Separate CORS_ONLY headers (no Content-Type) for 204/202 from JSON_HEADERS (with Content-Type) used on 200 responses.

workarounds.symptom: gcloud commands prompt 'Do you want to continue (Y/n)?' in headless terminal subprocesses, freezing execution until watchdog timeout.
workarounds.workaround: Always append '--quiet' flag to every gcloud CLI invocation (e.g. 'gcloud compute instances stop <name> --quiet').

workarounds.symptom: FastMCP python sidecar on Windows can emit CRLF line endings on stdio transport, corrupting JSON-RPC framing in strict MCP clients.
workarounds.workaround: Configure sys.stdout to binary write mode (sys.stdout.reconfigure(newline='\n')) or switch to remote Streamable HTTP transport.

workarounds.symptom: ESLint v9 deprecates .eslintrc.* legacy format. Running 'eslint .' fails with 'ESLint couldn't find an eslint.config.(js|mjs|cjs) file'.
workarounds.workaround: Migrate to flat config 'eslint.config.mjs' exporting an array of configuration objects, or set ESLINT_USE_FLAT_CONFIG=false for legacy projects.

workarounds.symptom: Docker CLI invokes 'docker-credential-desktop.exe' on Windows when ~/.docker/config.json contains 'credsStore': 'desktop', throwing exit code 1 in background shells.
workarounds.workaround: Remove 'credsStore' from ~/.docker/config.json or pass explicit auth tokens to daemon.

workarounds.symptom: Cloudflare Pages Functions greedy catch-all router (functions/[[route]].js) intercepts GET requests for static CDN assets, returning 404 or 405.
workarounds.workaround: In functions router, inspect request.method: if GET/HEAD, delegate immediately to 'env.ASSETS.fetch(request)'.

workarounds.symptom: mastra @mastra/core@1.78.0: Fixed revoked or invalid OAuth sign-ins showing a raw API error. When Anthropic, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot, xAI, or Kimi For Coding rejects a stored sign-in with a 401, the erro
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Fixed revoked or invalid OAuth sign-ins showing a raw API error. When Anthropic, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot, xAI, or Kimi For Coding rejects a stored sign-in with a 401, the error is now a `ProviderAuthRequiredError` that says the sign-in was rejected, the same as a missing sign-in. Hosts can match on the error name to prompt the user to sign in again. (#27187). Upstream PR #27187. (Ref: https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/27187)

workarounds.symptom: mastra @mastra/core@1.78.0: Fixed `FileTransport` and `UpstashTransport` log queries accepting invalid `page`/`perPage` values. `listLogs` and `listLogsByRunId` now throw a `RangeError` for negative, fraction

workarounds.symptom: [BUG] Interrupted RWLock acquisition releases a lock it never acquired
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(utilities): keep rwlock ownership when acquire is interrupted. Target files: lib/crewai/src/crewai/utilities/rw_lock.py, lib/crewai/tests/utilities/events/test_rw_lock.py. `r_locked()` and `w_locked()` called acquire inside the `try` that always releases in `finally`. If `Condition.wait()` is interrupted before acquire finishes, the context manager releases a lock it never held. The reader count can drop below zero, and the writer flag can be cleared while another writer still owns the lock. (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/7944)

workarounds.symptom: trulens trulens-2.15.0: **Feedback callback failures are logged** — `run_and_call_callback` returned from a `finally` block, discarding any exception the `on_done` callback raised, including a failed `add
workarounds.workaround: Fix: **Feedback callback failures are logged** — `run_and_call_callback` returned from a `finally` block, discarding any exception the `on_done` callback raised, including a failed `add_feedback` write. Failures are now logged, and `KeyboardInterrupt` and other `BaseException`s are no longer swallowed. (#2819) by @YHC66. Upstream PR #2819. (Ref: https://github.com/truera/trulens/pull/2819)

workarounds.symptom: trulens trulens-2.15.0: **The trace reaches HTTP/protobuf-only backends.** `otel_exporter="otlp"` only ever built gRPC exporters, so an HTTP/protobuf-only OTLP endpoint failed with a missing-dependency `I
workarounds.workaround: Fix: **The trace reaches HTTP/protobuf-only backends.** `otel_exporter="otlp"` only ever built gRPC exporters, so an HTTP/protobuf-only OTLP endpoint failed with a missing-dependency `ImportError`. `TruSession` now takes `otlp_protocol` (`"grpc"` or `"http/protobuf"`), honors `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL` and `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_PROTOCOL`, and still defaults to gRPC. Client hooks gain the matching `TRULENS_OTLP_PROTOCOL` variable and a new `TRULENS_DESTINATION=ai_gateway` for Snowflake Cortex AI Gateways, which serve OTLP over HTTP/protobuf only; `make_ai_gateway_otel_exporter()` in `trulens.connectors.snowflake.otel_exporter` builds the same exporter for connector users. Hook export failures are now logged with turn, client, and conversation context instead of being swallowed by the journal worker. (#2785) by @sfc-gh-jreini. Upstream PR #2785. (Ref: https://github.com/truera/trulens/pull/2785)

workarounds.symptom: trulens trulens-2.15.0: **Pre-OTel leaderboard no longer crashes** — `get_leaderboard_aggregates()` raised `NotImplementedError` whenever OTEL tracing was disabled, because the SQL used JSON subscripts on
workarounds.workaround: Fix: **Pre-OTel leaderboard no longer crashes** — `get_leaderboard_aggregates()` raised `NotImplementedError` whenever OTEL tracing was disabled, because the SQL used JSON subscripts on `TEXT` columns and referenced a nonexistent `Record.latency` column. Aggregation now happens in Python using the existing extraction helpers. (#2730) by @Aftabbs. Upstream PR #2730. (Ref: https://github.com/truera/trulens/pull/2730)

(#2806) by @YHC66. Upstream PR #2393. (Ref: https://github.com/truera/trulens/pull/2393)

workarounds.symptom: Casting `large_string` / `string_view` to ClassLabel fails, so `Dataset.from_pandas(df, features=ClassLabel)` breaks with pandas 3
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Fix Json.cast_storage double-encoding large_string and string_view columns. Target files: src/datasets/features/features.py, tests/features/test_features.py. `Json.cast_storage` only treats a `pa.StringArray` as already holding JSON text. `large_string` and `string_view` arrays are not subclasses of it, so they fall through to the generic branch and every value gets JSON-encoded a second time. The column then decodes back to plain strings instead of objects, and no error is raised. (Ref: https://github.com/huggingface/datasets/pull/8682)

Target files: docs/client/identity-assertion.md, examples/snippets/clients/identity_assertion_client.py, examples/snippets/servers/identity_assertion_server.py. The SDK only lets confidential clients (ones with a shared secret) use the ID-JAG `jwt-bearer` grant, on both the client provider and the built-in authorization server. Target files: tests/shared/test_path_security.py. `test_safe_join_rejects_symlink_escape` called `symlink_to()` unguarded. Windows only allows that for elevated processes or with Developer Mode on, so on an ordinary Windows dev machine the test errored with `WinError 1314` before it ever reached `safe_join`. CI didn't notice because the hosted Windows runners are allowed to create symlinks. (Ref: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/pull/3609)

workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(internvit): allocate pinned input buffers on demand. Target files: src/turbomind/models/internvit/internvit.cc. InternViT previously preallocated pinned input buffers using max_forward_token_num as the image batch capacity, causing unnecessarily large allocations at startup. workarounds.symptom: SSE stream drops the final event (finish_reason / response.completed lost) when the server omits the trailing blank line
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(streaming): emit terminal SSE events missing a trailing blank line. Target files: src/core/streaming.ts, tests/lib/streaming-core.test.ts. - `SSEDecoder` previously emitted only on a blank line. `iterSSEChunks` already yields leftover bytes at EOF and `LineDecoder` is flushed, but the SSE decoder was never flushed, so a final `data:` / `event:` record without `\n\n` was discarded. - Flush the pending SSE event at EOF so `finish_reason` / `response.completed` are delivered when a gateway closes the stream immediately a... (Ref: https://github.com/openai/openai-node/pull/2726)

workarounds.symptom: dify 1.17.1: **A plugin could exhaust worker memory with one declared number.** The blob chunk merger pre-allocated a buffer of the plugin-declared total length before checking it against the f
workarounds.workaround: Fix: **A plugin could exhaust worker memory with one declared number.** The blob chunk merger pre-allocated a buffer of the plugin-declared total length before checking it against the file size limit, so a plugin claiming an absurd size crashed the worker with `MemoryError` — the 30 MB limit was never consulted. The declared size is now validated first and rejected with the documented size-limit error. (#42021). Upstream PR #42021. (Ref: https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/42021)

workarounds.symptom: dify 1.17.1: **Any PDF loaded from a URL crashed with a bare `AssertionError`.** After tenant context was added to the PDF extractor, the code path used by `load_from_url` — including the built
workarounds.workaround: Fix: **Any PDF loaded from a URL crashed with a bare `AssertionError`.** After tenant context was added to the PDF extractor, the code path used by `load_from_url` — including the built-in web scraper whenever a target returns `Content-Type: application/pdf` — asserted on an upload record that URL loads never have. Tenant context is now optional, image extraction is skipped when it is absent, and text extraction works again. (#41950). Upstream PR #41950. (Ref: https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/41950)

workarounds.symptom: A node that is both a declared root and a child of another root runs multiple times, and KeyErrors in async
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(dag): reject a root node that is reachable from another root. Target files: deepeval/metrics/dag/graph.py, tests/test_metrics/test_dag.py. Declaring a node as a root when it's also a child of another root gives it two ways in, so the runner visits it once per path. In sync mode the whole subtree runs again, which means the same LLM calls are made and the cost is counted twice over. In async mode it doesn't get that far — it raises `KeyError` while looking up the node's parent. (Ref: https://github.com/confident-ai/deepeval/pull/3027)

workarounds.symptom: Gateway models send invalid strict JSON schemas for nested pydantic models
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(models): set additionalProperties recursively for gateway schemas. Target files: deepeval/models/llms/gateway_model.py, tests/test_core/test_models/test_openrouter_model.py. `DeepEvalOpenAICompatibleModel._schema_response_format` builds `response_format` by hand and sets `additionalProperties: false` only on the **root** schema object: (Ref: https://github.com/confident-ai/deepeval/pull/2930)

workarounds.symptom: Conversational datasets fail to serialize ToolCall enums
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(dataset): serialize tool call enums in JSON mode. Target files: deepeval/dataset/utils.py, tests/test_core/test_datasets/test_dataset.py. Dataset saves fail when a `ToolCall` contains its default `ToolCallType` enum because Python-mode Pydantic dumps leave the enum object for `json.dumps()`. (Ref: https://github.com/confident-ai/deepeval/pull/2926)

workarounds.symptom: Silent answer mis-scoring in MathQA, DROP, and BigBenchHard benchmarks (correct answers scored 0)
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(benchmarks): correct silent answer mis-scoring in MathQA, DROP, and BigBenchHard. Target files: deepeval/benchmarks/big_bench_hard/big_bench_hard.py, deepeval/benchmarks/drop/drop.py, deepeval/benchmarks/math_qa/math_qa.py. While auditing the benchmark answer-scoring paths, I found **three silent bugs** — cases where a **correct** prediction is scored `0` with no error raised, systematically deflating reported benchmark accuracy. Each is reproduced below and covered by an offline regression test that fails on the c... (Ref: https://github.com/confident-ai/deepeval/pull/2916)

workarounds.symptom: OpenAI `gpt-image-2` errors on `input_fidelity`
workarounds.workaround: Fix: openai: omit `input_fidelity` when `None` in image generation tool. Target files: pydantic_ai_slim/pydantic_ai/models/openai.py, tests/models/test_openai_responses.py. OpenAI's `gpt-image-2` model rejects requests that include `input_fidelity: null`. Pydantic AI was unconditionally passing `input_fidelity` to the OpenAI Responses API even when the user had not explicitly set it, causing a 400 error for `gpt-image-2` users. (Ref: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/pull/5415)

workarounds.symptom: BUG: f-string escape error in ToolSerializer.dumps causes uninformative error message
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix: correct f-string escaping in ToolSerializer.dumps error message. Target files: src/smolagents/serialization.py. `ToolSerializer.dumps()` line 429 uses double braces `{{e}}` in the f-string, producing a literal `{e}` instead of interpolating the exception. Line 292 in the same file has the correct single-brace form. (Ref: https://github.com/huggingface/smolagents/pull/2134)

workarounds.symptom: [Bug]: Memory leak: AgentWorkflow stores heavy objects in ContextVar, pinned by asyncio task Context snapshots
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Fix memory leak from copied RunContext. Target files: packages/llama-index-workflows/src/workflows/runtime/control_loop.py, packages/llama-index-workflows/src/workflows/runtime/types/plugin.py, packages/llama-index-workflows/tests/test_workflow.py. asyncio `TimerHandle`s capture the current `Context` at schedule time, which pinned the workflow's `RunContext` ContextVar until the timer fired.
